newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-COSTA AND MOYA KEEP DAVIS CUP PLACES FOR GERMANY TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COSTA AND MOYA KEEP DAVIS CUP PLACES FOR GERMANY TIE.

text.p: Alberto Costa and Carlos Moya have retained their Davis Cup singles places for Spain's tie against Germany next month after putting in fine performances in the Australian Open.
In doubles, an area where Spain have had problems in recent seasons, Alex Corretja will team up with Carlos Costa, who replaces Tomas Carbonell for the world group first-round tie.

The interest generated by Moya's splendid run in Melbourne, where he has reached the semifinals, has not gone unnoticed in his home town of Palma de Mallorca, where the tie will be held from February 7 to 9.
Ticket sales for the event picked up dramatically after the announcement of the team on Wednesday afternoon.

But the choice of venue has generated considerable controversy in Spain. Several Spanish players feel that their home advantage will be lost by playing on the holiday island, which has a strong German expatriate community.
But Germany will definitely start as underdogs as both their leading singles players -- Boris Becker and Michael Stich -- have said they will miss the tie.
